name: ICON plc
moat_justification: A narrow, scale-based moat. ICON is one of the few CROs that can run a global late-phase program, contracted trials are hard to move mid-study, and the $21.8B backlog gives revenue visibility — that earns a moderate score. But the measured returns cap it: after the $12B PRA Health acquisition (closed July 2021), roic_proxy in fundamentals.json ran 2.4% / 5.5% / 7.0% / 7.7% / 3.5% for FY2021-25 versus 25.2% in FY2020 pre-deal, and gross margin sat at ~29% for FY2020-24 (fundamentals.json) with FY2025 direct costs of $6,075,746,000 rising against nearly flat revenue — a franchise earning below its cost of capital through the cycle does not get 7+. Sponsors hold the pricing power, cancellations are a standing feature, and the 2025-26 revenue-recognition restatement damaged the trust a services moat runs on. Moat 5/10, CAP 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-05-27), cover page: securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b) are 'ORDINARY SHARES, PAR VALUE €0.06 EACH', trading symbol ICLR, NASDAQ Global Select Market — the traded security is the ordinary share itself, not an ADS representing multiple shares) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
one_liner: Scale CRO with a narrow moat 5/10 and post-PRA returns below the cost of capital — does not clear 15% at $170.18 (weighted IRR 8.0%, IV@15% $76.24 vs $170.18 price); even the super-bull case returns only 12.7%, and 2026 is guided down — clears 15% only below ~$76.
moat_for: Scale: one of the two largest global CROs, ~$8.25B revenue and a $21.8B backlog at Dec 31, 2025 ($23.4B at Jun 30, 2026) — sponsors shortlist only a handful of CROs that can run global Phase II-III programs
Mid-trial switching costs are real: replacing a CRO mid-study risks timelines, data continuity and regulatory filings, so contracted work is sticky once running

Strategic partnerships and FSP (functional service provider) embedding inside large pharma R&D organisations, plus labs, site networks and decentralised-trial capability built through the PRA acquisition
Cash conversion is structurally strong: owner's earnings positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, FY2025 operating cash flow $1,036M against capex of only $174M (asset-light, people-based model)
moat_against: Post-PRA returns are weak: roic_proxy 2.4% (FY2021), 5.5% (FY2022), 7.0% (FY2023), 7.7% (FY2024), 3.5% (FY2025) — below the cost of capital since the $12B deal; the earnings power the returns measure is people and contracts, not owned assets
Gross margin is thin and slipping: ~29% FY2020-24, ~26.4% in FY2025 on the 20-F direct-cost line, with direct costs growing faster than revenue

Trials can be cancelled or delayed by sponsors: FY2025 cancellations $2,834M under the new policy, Q3 2025 management cited elevated cancellations and delayed decision-making; backlog was cut $3.9B by a policy change alone (to $21.1B at Oct 1, 2025)
Contested oligopoly: IQVIA (larger data assets), Thermo Fisher/PPD, Medpace (higher margins in biotech) and sponsor in-sourcing / FSP price pressure

Credibility damage: Audit Committee investigation found improper revenue-timing adjustments overstating FY2023 revenue by $65M and FY2024 by $93M, with material weaknesses in internal controls still being remediated through 2026
